clue.text: Help because one is after second position

indicators.note: one is placed after second, so the letter for one follows the abbreviation for second

parts.note: as can mean because, as in 'as it was raining'
the Roman numeral for one is I
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Someone offers help, explaining that they come after whoever is in second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is a direct synonym for help or aid given to someone.

clue.text: A fine line cut for hairstyle

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: cut means the word for line loses its final letter

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A thin line trimmed into a haircut, as a barber might shave a parting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of ROW, leaving RO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: Singer's singular work performed with love

definitions.note: Singer's stands for 'singer is', the definition followed by a link

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
OP is short for opus, a musical work
ran can mean performed or operated, as a machine ran
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A singer is performing a solo work with great love.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Singer's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice range.

clue.text: Strangely uncivil around start of Peasants' Revolt

indicators.note: around tells us the word for uncivil wraps the other pieces

parts.note: surly means rude or uncivil

indicators.note: start of takes just the opening letter of Peasants'

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or uprising

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly rude behaviour surrounds the beginning of the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition. The Peasants' Revolt was a 1381 English uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean in an unexpected or astonishing way.

clue.text: Fizzy drink flips containing most of said fruit

indicators.note: containing means the turned drink holds the other piece inside it
flips means the word for fizzy drink turns over, reading the other way in this down clue

parts.note: soda is a fizzy drink

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word for said

parts.note: vocal means said aloud, voiced

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink can is flipped over, holding most of the fruit mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips' turns the drink to ADOS. 'said' looks like a link to the fruit, but means spoken, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocados are pear-shaped fruits with a large stone and buttery flesh.

clue.text: Mutt set on angry tailless pointer

indicators.note: in a down clue, set on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, a mutt

indicators.note: tailless removes the last letter of the word for angry

parts.note: sore is informal for angry or annoyed

explanation.surface: A mongrel dog is set upon an angry pointer dog that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutt' and 'pointer' look like a pair of dogs; pointer is the computer screen arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursor is the movable pointer on a computer screen.

clue.text: For example, very big personalities

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very big

explanation.surface: Celebrities with very large personalities are mentioned as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is a person's sense of self, so egos are personalities or selves.

clue.text: Musician finally wearing vulgar decoration

indicators.note: wearing means the word for vulgar has the musician's last letter inside it, as a garment holds its wearer

parts.note: garish means gaudy, showy or vulgar

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of Musician

explanation.surface: A musician is dressed in tasteless, flashy ornamentation.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a decorative touch, especially one added to food.

clue.text: Endless row raised about American prison's hanging

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the remaining pieces
raised means the trimmed word is read upwards in this down clue
Endless drops the final letter of the word for row

parts.note: row in the sense of din or racket is noise
US is short for United States, American
pen is slang for penitentiary, a prison; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A noisy dispute arises about an American prison's use of execution by hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims NOISE to NOIS; 'raised' turns it to SION, which goes 'about' US and PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is something hung, as a chandelier is in suspension, so it means hanging.

clue.text: Queen record, i.e. retro remix, for collection

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: remix says the letters of these two words are mixed up again

parts.note: the letters of the abbreviation i.e. as written

explanation.surface: A Queen record mixes up a retro track, presented as a compilation album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band but gives R. 'remix' rearranges IE and RETRO into ERTOIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertoire is the stock of pieces a performer has ready, a collection of works.

clue.text: A marine force's weaponry

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines, the British naval infantry force, and the possessive gives an S

explanation.surface: A naval force shows off its weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms means weapons collectively, as in an arms dealer.

clue.text: Beef, meat and greens I'd cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

parts.note: the letters of I'd, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A recipe of beef, meat and vegetables that I have cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' sits beside meat and greens as food, but it is slang for a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a complaint or quarrel, a falling-out between people.

clue.text: Pretty good place for entertainment

definitions.meaning: reasonably good, moderate, as in a decent result
a funfair, with rides and stalls

explanation.definitionFit: The word means moderately good, and is also a travelling show of rides and amusements.

clue.text: Native American carried round single spirit

indicators.note: round means the word for carried goes around the other pieces

parts.note: bore is the past tense of bear, to carry
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A Native American takes a single drink of spirit around with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Native' alone and American gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, a native.

clue.text: Ultimate in care among poorly tots and cribs?

definitions.text: Ultimate in care among poorly tots and cribs?

indicators.note: among puts that letter in with the rearranged letters
poorly suggests the letters are out of sorts and rearranged
Ultimate in takes the final letter of care

explanation.surface: Top-quality medical care for sick infants lying in their cots.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the medical field: care around babies and cots.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics is the branch of medicine dealing with childbirth and newborn care.

clue.text: Setting where volume can be turned up?

definitions.text: Setting where volume can be turned up?

parts.words: Setting where volume can be turned up?
parts.note: volume means a book rather than loudness, and turned up means found on a shelf

explanation.surface: A place where you can crank up the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling books is where a particular volume might turn up.

clue.text: Misery created by 'snip' at hospital

indicators.note: created by says the answer is made from letters running across the following words

explanation.surface: Suffering caused by a vasectomy performed in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snip' suggests a small operation, but the letters run through snip, at and hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is a quality evoking pity or sadness, close to misery or suffering.

clue.text: Cut a pork pie consumed around North

indicators.note: around means the first pieces go round the letter for North

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Slicing a pork pie that someone has eaten up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: pork pie rhymes with lie. 'Cut' is the verb to snub someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, turning them away or estranging them.

clue.text: Toilet commonly found in shed, we hear

definitions.note: commonly marks the informal slang use of the word for toilet

indicators.note: we hear signals that the clue word is matched by its spoken sound

parts.note: shed means cast off, as a horse throws or sheds a rider

explanation.surface: An outside lavatory is found in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building, but it is the past participle of shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Throne is a jokey colloquial name for the lavatory seat.

clue.text: Rodent exterminator catching large snake

indicators.note: catching means the exterminator holds the letter for large inside it

parts.note: a ratter is a dog or person that kills rats

explanation.surface: A pest controller catches a huge snake instead of a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is short for rattlesnake, a venomous American snake.

clue.text: Criminal clears off losing tail outside

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape
losing tail drops the last letter of off

explanation.surface: A criminal clears off, giving the police the slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' looks like shaking off a pursuer, but trims OFF to OF; 'Criminal' rearranges CLEARS plus OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, outdoors.

clue.text: 'Game's up!', remorsefully admits leader

indicators.note: admits means the phrase lets the answer in, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: A ringleader caught out confesses with remorse that the game is up.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, a boss.

clue.text: A jester somersaulting over popular knight

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the turned pieces sit above the next one
somersaulting means these two pieces flip and read the other way

parts.note: a wag is a joker or jester
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A court jester tumbles over a well-liked knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaulting' turns A WAG into GAWA. Gawain is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain was one of King Arthur's knights of the Round Table.

clue.text: Tease bird I left behind

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Teasing a bird that I left trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse teasingly.

clue.text: Glimpse end of eternity by sixth sense

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, the sixth sense

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of eternity

explanation.surface: A glimpse of the end of eternity, seen through a sixth sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to glimpse.

clue.text: Idiot frames thousand questions

indicators.note: frames means the word for idiot surrounds the letter for thousand

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: A fool sets up a thousand questions.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense: asks means questions, enquires of someone.

clue.text: Work-shy indulged, oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of indulged

explanation.surface: A lazy person, indulged in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes someone lazy who avoids work.

clue.text: Team with spare over taking runs, boundaries

indicators.note: taking means the rearranged letters hold the letter for runs
over suggests the letters are turned over and rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket team with a spare player over takes runs and hits boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface points 'boundaries' at fours and sixes, but it means limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Parameters are limits or bounds within which something operates.

clue.text: Small boat leading to island

parts.note: an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A small boat heading for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small island in the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Catching fine cut is fantastic taking over

indicators.note: taking means the rearranged letters hold the letter for over
fantastic suggests a wild rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A fine cut is fantastic for taking over a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching describes a disease that spreads, contagious.
